newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - U.S. data release sends Bund vols down.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - U.S. data release sends Bund vols down.

text.p: Implied volatility of Bund options traded on LIFFE fell on Friday, following the release of U.S. inflation data, traders said.

"Bund futures swung wildly on the data, which left the options pit pretty quiet while things sorted themselves out," said a trader at a British brokerage on LIFFE. "When options got going after the data, volatility pushed down quickly."
U.S. producer prices fell 0.1 percent in March compared with a 0.4 percent drop in February. Core PPI rose 0.4 percent versus a 0.1 percent fall in the previous month.
March retail sales rose a lower than expected 0.2 percent, compared to a revised 1.5 percent increase in February.
At 1420 GMT June Bunds were trading down 23 basis points at 99.88, off more than half a point from 100.31 before the data.

May straddles were trading at a volatility of 4.7 percent, off from 5.35/45 earlier in the session. Traders said the sharp nature of the move was owing to the proximity of the April 23 expiry of May serial options on the June Bund future.
"This was the last big figure before the expiry, and on top of that there are two days to knock off for the weekend," said a trader, referring to time decay.

June volatility was trading at 5.45 percent, compared with 5.65 percent before the data were released. Traders said it had been offered for much of the session, but trade had remained very quiet as investors had hedged against the figures earlier in the week.
